tier_rationale: The manufacturer's own shared owner's manual for the EU2200i / EU2200i Companion line prints two distinct wiring diagrams: the base 'AG, AN TYPE' diagram has no radio component at all, while the 'AG1, AN1 TYPE' diagram (the Companion variant) shows a discrete 'BLUETOOTH UNIT' wired into the control panel. The manual states the My Generator app works 'only with Honda generators equipped with Bluetooth technology' — the base EU2200i is not one of them.
the_unplug_test: This generator has no network to lose. It is a pull-start (or optional electric-start) engine, an inverter, and a control panel with an oil-alert light and an eco-throttle switch. The base wiring diagram contains no Bluetooth module at all — only the EU2200i Companion variant has the radio soldered in — so there is no app, no pairing, and nothing that changes behavior whether or not any network exists nearby.

repairability.notes: Widely serviced by Honda Power Equipment dealers; spark plug, oil, and air filter are user-serviceable per the manual's maintenance schedule.

sources.supports: Manufacturer owner's manual for EU2200i / EU2200i Companion: specifications table lists both models side by side (Generator 'Type' AG/AG3/AN/AN3 for base EU2200i vs AG1/AN1 for Companion); the wiring diagram section prints a separate 'AG, AN TYPE' schematic with no radio component, and an 'AG1, AN1 TYPE' schematic that adds a labeled 'BLUETOOTH UNIT' block. Text states the My Generator app functions (remote stop, monitoring, notifications) work 'only with Honda generators equipped with Bluetooth technology.'
Independent corroboration that standard EU2200i units do not have Bluetooth and that only the EU2200i Companion (EU2200iC) ships with the built-in Bluetooth radio for the My Generator app.

open_questions: FCC grantee search for Honda Motor Co. (grantee prefixes including N43) was inconclusive within budget — did not turn up a specific grant for the Companion's Bluetooth unit to use as an explicit sibling-grant citation, though the manual's own wiring diagrams are direct manufacturer evidence and were treated as sufficient.

Honda's model-number suffixes (T, TAG1, TAN1, etc.) encode electric-start, parallel-ready, and Companion/Bluetooth options in ways that are easy to buy the wrong variant of — a buyer should check the generator 'Type' code (AG/AN = no radio, AG1/AN1 = Bluetooth) on the spec plate or box, not just the headline 'EU2200i' name.
notes: A clean within-model-line split: Honda sells the base EU2200i and the Bluetooth-equipped EU2200i Companion under nearly the same name and the same manual, distinguished only by a wiring-diagram-level 'Type' code. This is the model-number pattern SCOUT flags as highest-yield: the dumb option sits on the shelf next to its connected sibling.
